traits.flowering_months.note: iNaturalist research-grade records on GBIF in the south and central Puget Sound lowlands (46.7 to 48.0° N, 122.0 to 123.1° W; counted 2026-10-14): 81 records annotated as flowering (Apr 1, May 52, Jun 21, Jul 6, Nov 1); stated as the months holding at least a tenth of them, May and June. FEIS (Rosa nutkana) gives May to July.

traits.fruiting_months.note: FEIS (Rosa nutkana): hips ripen in early fall and stay on the plant through the winter (the Seed Manual says the same of roses); so ripe hips are on the plant from September to February.

generator.params.path_half.note: A choice of the model's (crown form step B, broadleaf revision 11): the wood from the base at which a shoot's nodes are half as long, fitted so the plant grows to the height of its oldest reference size, with the crown's width left to grow inside the loose region.

generator.params.note: Hand-set from general knowledge of the species: a prickly shrub of upright stems with pinnate leaves of toothed leaflets and large single pink flowers, followed by round red hips. Not fitted to measurements.

allometry.note: Rough sizes from general knowledge of the species: 1.5 m tall at 12 years in the open. Replace with measured data before calling this species calibrated.

appearance.note: Colours chosen by eye: mid-green leaflets; pink flowers; reddish-brown stems. Fruit (plant roadmap P4), as in mid-July: round hips about 2 cm across with the sepals still on, green turning red. Its year (appearance.organs.bloom.season) takes its days of bud, flower, fruit, ripe and fall from the months it flowers and fruits in, by the rules at the flowering plants (development, 2026-10-14); until then they were authored from general knowledge of the species in the south Puget Sound lowlands: pink roses in May to July; hips green, red from August, hanging through the winter. The forest's packages show day 196 (mid-July) until the phenology of plant roadmap P5 sets the day from the date and the local climate.

taxon.note: Scientific and common names (and USDA symbol, where given) as the spec's authors wrote them, and the genus the scientific name is written in.

growth_form.note: The growth form the spec's authors chose from the plant's habit.

growth.note: The growth plan (years, step, keyframes) chosen for growing and rendering, not a botanical fact.

variants.note: The environments, conditions and seeds chosen for growing and rendering, not a botanical fact.

taxon.family.note: WCVP v16's family for the accepted name.

taxon.plant_name_id.note: WCVP v16's plant_name_id for the accepted species the name resolves to (the accepted name).

appearance.organs.bloom.season.flower_lo.note: Its flower laid out whorl by whorl (spec rework P5): five petals and five sepals on a hypanthium, from the characters of Rosaceae by the rules at the flowering plants. By hand (as search results quote them; the pages themselves were not read): the sepals nearly as long as the petals (the USDA's plant guide); 60 stamens and 20 pistils for the floras' many stamens and more than ten pistils (Ertter).
